verdict.rationale: Vercel's Limits page documents hard API rate limits with a per-action table, platform caps such as concurrent deployments, and per-plan function duration and memory/CPU limits. The REST API also exposes X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset headers, so API rate limits are well covered. Function concurrency caps, however, are not documented as a concrete limit: Fluid compute is only described as scaling concurrency. missing for 10: a documented per-function concurrency cap (max concurrent instances or invocations per plan), and independent or hands-on corroboration of the published limits.

support.subject: As a developer, I know the documented rate limits and concurrency caps for APIs and functions so I can plan for scale

citations.quote: Rate limits are hard limits that apply to the platform when performing actions that require a response from our API.
Rate limits are specified via response headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, and X-RateLimit-Reset
Memory and CPU: 2 GB / 1 vCPU default and max [Hobby] / 2 GB / 1 vCPU default, up to 4 GB / 2 vCPU max [Pro and Enterprise]
